title: Go: Logging
description: Use Go's log package for structured logging, custom loggers, and output control.

steps.title: log.Println
steps.description: Use `log.Println("Application started")` to print a log message. Print also `log.Printf("User %s logged in", "Alice")`. Note the default timestamp prefix.
hints: `log.Println` works like fmt.Println but adds timestamp
Output includes date and time automatically

verification.failureMessage: Use log.Println and log.Printf to print messages.

steps.title: log.Fatalf
steps.description: Write a function `connectDB(dsn string)` that calls `log.Fatalf("Failed to connect: %s", err)` if the dsn is empty. Call with an empty string and note the exit behavior.
hints: It's useful for fatal initialization errors

verification.successMessage: Fatalf logged and exited on fatal error!
verification.failureMessage: Call log.Fatalf with a format string and arguments.

steps.title: SetPrefix and SetFlags
steps.description: Configure the default logger: set prefix to "[MYAPP] " using `log.SetPrefix` and set flags to `log.Lshortfile | log.Ltime` using `log.SetFlags`. Then log "Configuration loaded".
hints: Available flags: Ldate, Ltime, Lmicroseconds, Llongfile, Lshortfile, LUTC

verification.successMessage: Custom log prefix and flags applied!
verification.failureMessage: Set prefix and flags before calling the log function.

steps.title: Log to a file
steps.description: Create a file "app.log" using `os.Create`. Create a logger with `log.New(file, "LOG: ", log.LstdFlags)`. Log 3 messages: "Starting", "Processing", and "Done". Print "Logged to app.log".
hints: `log.New(io.Writer, prefix, flags)` creates a custom logger
Open the file with os.Create or os.OpenFile
Each log message goes to the file, not stdout

verification.failureMessage: Use log.New with the file handle as the writer.

steps.title: Custom logger with io.Writer
steps.description: Create a custom logger that writes to multiple destinations using `io.MultiWriter`. Write to both stdout and a file. Log "Multi-writer log" and verify it appears in both.
hints: The message appears on both outputs

verification.successMessage: Multi-writer logger sends to stdout and file!
verification.failureMessage: Use io.MultiWriter to combine multiple writers.
